name: code-review

description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

name: compass
description: Find which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. Use when you (or the agent) are unsure which skill to reach for, want to see how the skills fit together, or ask "what should I use for X".

Use to re-conform an adopted repo as guidance evolves, or as a step inside adopt-project. Trigger: conformance audit, check repo against standards, re-conform, does this repo still follow current conventions."

name: curate-docs
description: "Review docs/agents and .scratch for promotion and deletion: graduate mature notes into skills, move reference docs into a skill's references, and prune stale or superseded material."

name: diagnosing-bugs
description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

name: domain-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model (app/backend/business software). Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording an ADR. For a game's real-time systems and design model, use game-modeling instead.

name: game-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a game's design model, mechanics, systems, and the core loop. Use when discussing game mechanics or terminology, writing a mechanics glossary, or recording a design decision. For a game's backend/economy/meta (business software), use domain-modeling instead.

name: game-native-design
description: Build games that feel like games, not web apps. Use when designing or reviewing game code: the loop, simulation state, performance, feel, or when another skill needs the game-native vocabulary. Reach for the matching engine appendix once the engine is known.

name: grilling

name: tkt-core
description: "Track tasks as markdown files in your git repo. Use when managing tickets, checking the frontier (what's ready), claiming work, closing tasks, creating tickets, decomposing work into a task graph, or validating project health. Trigger: tkt, tickets, what to work on, create ticket, validate tickets, decompose, break into tasks, work breakdown, task graph, ticket format, blocked by, backlog, park this, defer."
compatibility: Requires git

name: tkt-orient
description: "Start-of-session pickup from the reconciled plan and tickets: read the frontier, in-progress threads, and plan ordering that tkt-reconcile left behind, flag stale WIP, and propose the next step. Use when starting a session, resuming after a break, or asking 'where were we?' / 'what's next?' / 'pick up where we left off'. Trigger: start of session, orient, resume, pick up where we left off, where were we, what's next, catch me up, continue, session start, what's on the board."

name: tkt-reconcile
description: "End-of-session ticket + plan pass: make every ticket current, capture all open work as tickets, and re-prioritize/re-sequence the plan to match current priorities and work streams. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, after planning, when work feels untracked, or asking 'is everything captured?' / 'update the plan'. Trigger: sync tickets, update the plan, re-prioritize, end of session ticket pass, ticket review, are tickets current, is everything tracked, ticket audit, ticket hygiene, wrap up tickets, tag scope, work stream."

name: tkt-work
description: "Claim and execute a ticket from the frontier: pick the next ready ticket, claim it, verify its premises against primary sources, do the work, verify acceptance criteria, and close with evidence. The execution loop between tkt-orient (propose) and tkt-reconcile (wrap up). Use when working a ticket, picking up the next task, or asked 'work the frontier' / 'do the next ticket' / 'start on NN'. Trigger: work the frontier, do the next ticket, pick up work, claim and work, start ticket, next on the frontier, work a ticket, execute ticket, close ticket with evidence."
compatibility: Requires git

name: verify-tkt-usage

name: cpu-perf-bench
description: "Profile CPU hardware and benchmark native programs across compilers on Windows. Use when identifying the CPU model/frequency from the CLI, measuring the invariant TSC frequency, verifying QueryPerformanceCounter's RDTSC-based math, instrumentation-profiling where time goes inside a program (per-block/per-phase breakdown), or building and timing a program (e.g. the Performance-Aware Programming haversine listings) under MSVC, Clang, and GCC to compare codegen."

  - computer_enhance
  - time program across compilers
  - instrumentation profiling
  - profiler

  - time consumption of parts
  - per-block breakdown
  - profiling overhead

name: research
description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

name: research-audit
description: Validate and score a research findings file against its sources. Use after research produces a findings file, or when the user wants a cited analysis checked for citation accuracy, source trust, and currency.

name: retro
description: "Conduct a retrospective on a coding session: read it from a fresh context and propose environment fixes (checks, guardrails, steering), classified mechanical vs judgement. Use when a session ends, after a build that went sideways, or when wrap-session reaches its retro step."

disable-model-invocation: true

name: spike-options
description: "Compare competing approaches with throwaway builds, then agree an integration plan. Use when a hard-to-reverse choice is cheap to spike and uncertainty needs observation rather than more reasoning: compare alternatives, spike options, test competing designs."

name: sync
description: "Pull grey-matter current and re-synchronize the coupled pieces — deployed skills, the tkt command surface, ticket IDs, and repo invariants — then redeploy. disable-model-invocation: true

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

name: teach

disable-model-invocation: true
argument-hint: "What would you like to learn about?"

name: tkt-core
description: "Track tasks as markdown files in your git repo. Use when managing tickets, checking the frontier (what's ready), claiming work, closing tasks, creating tickets, decomposing work into a task graph, or validating project health. Trigger: tkt, tickets, what to work on, create ticket, validate tickets, decompose, break into tasks, work breakdown, task graph, ticket format, blocked by, backlog, park this, defer."
compatibility: Requires git

name: tkt-orient
description: "Start-of-session pickup from the reconciled plan and tickets: read the frontier, in-progress threads, and plan ordering that tkt-reconcile left behind, flag stale WIP, and propose the next step. Use when starting a session, resuming after a break, or asking 'where were we?' / 'what's next?' / 'pick up where we left off'. Trigger: start of session, orient, resume, pick up where we left off, where were we, what's next, catch me up, continue, session start, what's on the board."

name: tkt-reconcile
description: "End-of-session ticket + plan pass: make every ticket current, capture all open work as tickets, and re-prioritize/re-sequence the plan to match current priorities and work streams. Use when wrapping up a session, auditing ticket health, after planning, when work feels untracked, or asking 'is everything captured?' / 'update the plan'. Trigger: sync tickets, update the plan, re-prioritize, end of session ticket pass, ticket review, are tickets current, is everything tracked, ticket audit, ticket hygiene, wrap up tickets, tag scope, work stream."

name: tkt-work
description: "Claim and execute a ticket from the frontier: pick the next ready ticket, claim it, verify its premises against primary sources, do the work, verify acceptance criteria, and close with evidence. Trigger: work the frontier, do the next ticket, pick up work, claim and work, start ticket, next on the frontier, work a ticket, execute ticket, close ticket with evidence."
compatibility: Requires git

name: to-spec

disable-model-invocation: true

name: triage
description: "Move external requests (issues, PRs) and internal tkt tickets through triage roles: categorise, verify with real evidence, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. Use when the user asks to triage issues or tickets, or when adopt-project seeds a board from raw items."

skills.name: grey-matter:code-review

skills.name: grey-matter:codebase-design

skills.name: grey-matter:compass
skills.description: Find which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. Use when you (or the agent) are unsure which skill to reach for, want to see how the skills fit together, or ask "what should I use for X".

skills.name: grey-matter:conformance-audit
skills.description: Audit a repo's skills, tool scripts, agent guidance, and docs against grey-matter's current standards, then apply the mechanically-safe fixes behind an approval gate. Trigger: conformance audit, check repo against standards, re-conform, does this repo still follow current conventions.

skills.name: grey-matter:curate-docs
skills.description: Review docs/agents and .scratch for promotion and deletion: graduate mature notes into skills, move reference docs into a skill's references, and prune stale or superseded material.

skills.name: grey-matter:delivery-dashboard

skills.name: grey-matter:diagnosing-bugs
